title: Wall Street Initiates SK Hynix Coverage With Bullish Calls, BofA Says Stock Is 'Deeply Mispriced'
excerpt: Six brokerages launched coverage of the recently U.S.-listed memory chipmaker with buy ratings, citing its dominance in AI-critical high-bandwidth memory chips and a valuation gap with rival Micron.
body:
• Six brokerages including BofA Global Research initiated coverage of SK Hynix with buy-equivalent ratings after its recent U.S. listing
  • Rosenblatt Securities set the highest price target at $320, implying more than 100% upside from current levels around $151
  • BofA called SK Hynix "deeply mispriced," citing strong orders from U.S. tech firms and leadership in high-bandwidth memory chips
  • The stock trades 16% below its $149 ADR listing price despite SK Hynix posting a record quarterly profit with 257% revenue growth

SK Hynix's recently listed American Depositary Receipts surged 5% on Tuesday after six Wall Street brokerages launched coverage of the South Korean memory chipmaker with bullish ratings, led by Bank of America's assessment that the stock is "deeply mispriced" relative to its AI-driven growth trajectory.

The ADRs, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker SKHY, closed at $150.08 — still 16% below their July 10 listing price of $149 per share, weighed down by a broader pullback in semiconductor stocks. SK Hynix raised roughly $26.5 billion in what became the largest-ever U.S. secondary listing by a foreign company, according to Reuters.

The Bull Case: AI Memory Dominance

BofA Global Research, which served as an underwriter for the offering alongside Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, and J.P. Morgan, initiated coverage with a buy rating. The bank said SK Hynix remains undervalued, pointing to strong orders from major U.S. technology companies, leadership in high-end high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, and expectations for what it called "super-cycle" earnings as AI infrastructure spending ramps up.

Rosenblatt Securities set the street-high price target at $320. Analysts at William Blair struck a similar tone, arguing that the U.S. listing provides an opportunity for SK Hynix shares to "re-rate closer to its U.S.-based rival Micron" as investors gain direct access to the company.

"We believe the U.S. listing provides an opportunity for SKHY shares to re-rate closer to its U.S.-based rival, which should compound with a more structural re-rating driven by longer-term visibility and strong tie-in to AI and data center end markets."

— William Blair Analysts

Record Profit, But a Miss on Expectations

The coverage initiations came on the heels of SK Hynix's Q2 earnings report, which showed a record quarterly profit on 257% year-over-year revenue growth. Operating profit surged 557%. But the results fell short of analyst forecasts due to delays in shipments of advanced memory products, rattling investors who had bid up expectations of near-300% growth.

The shortfall was attributed to timing and product mix shifts, including the ramp-up of next-generation HBM4 chips. SK Hynix began shipping HBM4 in Q2, with the full production ramp scheduled for the second half of the year. The company also disclosed 10 new long-term agreements with hyperscale cloud clients, signalling a structural shift from spot-market pricing to multiyear contracts.

The Premium Problem

Not everyone is rushing to buy. The ADRs have traded at a premium to SK Hynix's Seoul-listed common shares — at one point as high as 51%, according to The Motley Fool, citing a 2025 MSCI study that found the typical ADR premium ranges between 2% and 4%. That gap has narrowed from its peak but remains elevated compared to peers like Taiwan Semiconductor, whose ADR premium sits around 15%.

MarketBeat noted that the eroding premium is itself creating a buying opportunity, with the risk-reward profile improving as the stock pulls back from its $194.80 high. Across 40 analyst reports covering both the U.S. and Korean listings, the consensus reflects a Moderate Buy to Strong Buy with over 100% upside potential.

What to Watch

SK Hynix's trajectory depends on whether AI memory demand proves structural rather than cyclical. The company aims to double chip wafer capacity within five years, bolstered by a supply agreement with Nvidia valued at over $500 billion. HBM4 production ramp-up in the second half will be the near-term catalyst, along with any signals from hyperscaler capital expenditure plans. For investors, the question is not whether SK Hynix is an AI leader — but how much of that leadership is already in the price.
nri_angle: Indian-American tech investors and semiconductor watchers should note the valuation dynamics as SK Hynix's U.S. listing opens a new avenue for exposure to the AI memory trade.
